definitions.explanation: The rise and fall of sea water caused by gravitational forces. Also refers to the flow of ocean currents.
A favorable moment or turning point. Often used in the expression {潮|しお}どき (a good time to do something).

examples.japanese: {潮|しお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{満|み}ちて→満ちる：02428_michiru⟧きた。
{潮|しお}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{流|なが}れ→流れ：03504_nagare⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{速|はや}い→速い：00514_hayai⟧。

examples.english: When the tide goes out, you can pick up shellfish on the rocks.

examples.japanese: ⟦そろそろ→そろそろ：01259_sorosoro⟧{潮|しお}どきだ。
{引|ひ}き{際|ぎわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{潮|しお}どき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見極|みきわ}める→見極める：07171_mikiwameru⟧。
examples.english: To judge the right moment to withdraw.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長引|ながび}いて→長引く：14473_nagabiku⟧きた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{潮|しお}どき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}った→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: The meeting was dragging on, so I found the right moment and excused myself.

notes:
USAGE:
{潮|しお} refers to ocean tides and currents. Not to be confused with ⟦{塩|しお}→塩：00887_shio⟧ (salt), which is a homophone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {潮|しお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{満|み}ちる→満ちる：02428_michiru⟧: the tide comes in
- {潮|しお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{引|ひ}く→引く：01978_hiku⟧: the tide goes out
- {潮|しお}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{流|なが}れ→流れ：03504_nagare⟧: tidal current
- {潮|しお}どき: the right time, a good opportunity
- ⟦{潮|しお}{風|かぜ}→潮風：17591_shiokaze⟧: sea breeze

WRITING:
{潮|しお} can also be read as うしお, an older literary reading.
